reader.requirement: At --std 85, FUNCTION REVERSE of a class alphabetic or alphanumeric argument of length n >= 1 returns an n-character string whose position j holds argument-1's character at position n-j+1. The argument can be an alphabetic, alphanumeric, alphanumeric-edited or numeric-edited elementary item, a group item (an OCCURS DEPENDING ON group at its current length), a reference-modified item or a nonnumeric literal.

edition-consulted.switches: D8 window: sig.IntroducedIn (85 on the catalog row) > ctx.Edition.DialectLevel raises COBOL1502, RemovedIn raises the removal error; at --std 85 neither fires
numeric-function-identifier-operand-2002 is checked, but its category test is false for an alphanumeric function, so REVERSE is accepted wherever an identifier stands, at 85 as at 2023

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel/Edition/ConstructRegistry/DialectBehavior over IntrinsicRenderer.cs#RenderStringValue and CobolIntrinsics.Text.cs: no hits. The argument-class screen does not consult the edition.

citations.check: OK  §1989:A.2.38.4 RV1  (2.38.4 Returned Values)  the text is in RV1 ['the returned value is a character string of length n']
OK  §1989:A.2.38.3 AR1  (2.38.3 Arguments)  the text is in AR1 ['must be at least one character in length']

reader.notes: The runtime body reverses the argument's character array. The emitter passes the argument's current image (the ODO extent or the reference-modified view), so n is the argument's length. 1985 puts numeric-edited items in class alphanumeric, and the 2023-worded class table accepts them, so 85 needs no arm of its own.
reader.at-2023: rev1.cob prints the same output at --std 2023

refuter.evidence: RVG.cob at 85 = 2023: REVERSE of a group holding X, S9(4) COMP, S9(3) COMP-3, S99 and X equals REVERSE of its MOVE-copy into X(8), round-trips back to the same bytes (G2=+0258 G3=-012 G4=-12), LENGTH(REVERSE(G))=8; JUSTIFIED RIGHT item -> [BA   ]; TE(I) and the whole table; literal "A""B" -> B"A; nested in UPPER-CASE; as INSPECT TALLYING, STRING and UNSTRING sending operand; comparison pads with spaces. Refusals at 85: X"4142" and B"1" literals COBOL0900, COMP-3 item / numeric expression / integer function argument COBOL1627, A(1:0) COBOL2670, receiving positions (MOVE TO, STRING INTO, INSPECT REPLACING, ACCEPT) refused. REVERSE(ZERO) -> [0], REVERSE(ALL "XY") -> [YX]: a figurative not associated with a data item is one character, ALL literal is the literal's length (§1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3). REVERSE(CURRENT-DATE)(1:4) = reversed UTC offset (correct). cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.38.4 RV1; OK §1989:A.2.38.3 AR1; OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3 'the length of the string is one character'.
